scores.label: Problem Understanding
scores.strengths: The proposal exhibits deep domain familiarity with CDC reporting programs, APHL interoperability workflows, and public health data exchanges through subcontractor J Michael Consulting.
scores.weaknesses: In §20.2 and §30, the vendor acknowledges relying on offshore technical resources in Australia and New Zealand, directly contravening the State's explicit legal and security mandates.

scores.strengths: The proposal clearly outlines deliverables across software, migration, training, and documentation frameworks using established templates.
scores.weaknesses: In §8.3, the proposal vaguely suggests bringing forward AWS Quicksights without clearly defining whether this work is included in the project baseline.

scores.label: Pricing Clarity
scores.weaknesses: In §4.1, pricing figures are deferred to a later time with no itemized cost breakdown or total proposal cost provided.

scores.label: Timeline Clarity
scores.strengths: The proposal identifies phased work packages and structured implementation steps in a detailed work breakdown structure.
scores.weaknesses: In §33.2, the work breakdown structure outlines activities but lacks specific dates or duration estimates for any phase or milestone.

scores.label: Completeness vs. RFP Requirements
scores.strengths: 16 of 21 requirements addressed: r1 Hosting Model Disclosure, r2 SLA Compliance Confirmation, r3 ADA WCAG 2.1 Compliance, r4 Concurrent User Capacity, r7 Configurable Reporting Rules Engine, r8 Legacy Data Migration Strategy, r9 Implementation and User Training, r10 Transition In and Out Plan, r11 Comprehensive Solution Documentation, r12 SUITE Methodology Utilization, r13 Milestone Work Breakdown Structure, r14 In-Person Project Kickoff Meeting, r17 Application Response Time Standards, r18 Mandatory System-to-System Interfaces, r20 Data Encryption Standards, r21 Regulatory Standards Compliance.

scores.label: Tone & Persuasiveness
scores.strengths: The bidder partners with J Michael Consulting to articulate credible public health experience and specific Michigan-relevant health informatics context.
scores.weaknesses: In §20.2 and §30, the vendor demonstrates an unpersuasive, contradictory stance by requesting exceptions for offshore support while simultaneously asserting full agreement without exceptions.

scores.label: Risk/Assumptions Transparency
scores.strengths: The proposal provides a clear 'QLIMS Customisation and Configuration Risk Impact Statement' outlining architectural isolation and modularity as mitigations for custom developments.
scores.weaknesses: In §20.2, the proposal acknowledges using personnel located in Australia and New Zealand to perform Level 3 support without recognizing this as a direct violation of mandatory RFP constraints prohibiting offshore resources and offshore environment access.

citations.quote: We have team members in Australia and New Zealand who perform level 3 support and will also be working
Custom development is containerized and modular, isolating it from the core QLIMS source code and preventing unintended impacts

coverage.explanation: The proposal does not provide or mention a Software Bill of Materials for solution components.
coverage.fix: Add a Software Bill of Materials covering all solution components and dependencies to §20.4.

coverage.explanation: The proposal does not mention retaining contract financial and accounting records for seven years.
coverage.fix: Add a commitment to retain all contract financial and accounting records for seven years to §18.

coverage.proposalQuote: To use MiLogin with AWS Cognito, you would need to see if MiLogin supports SAML 2.0 or OIDC.
coverage.explanation: The proposal conditions MiLogin integration on protocol verification rather than committing to integrate with the environment.
coverage.fix: Confirm direct integration and identity federation between the proposed solution and the State's MiLogin environment.

coverage.proposalQuote: QLIMS maintains a completed audit trail of all actions on any particular record including by which user and when
coverage.explanation: The proposal confirms auditing record actions by user and time but omits user location tracking.
coverage.fix: Confirm that the audit trail captures user location and specific system functions accessed by each user.

coverage.proposalQuote: 31.2 Background Checks — Bidder agrees with no exception.
coverage.explanation: The proposal agrees generally to background checks but does not provide required ICHAT or drug certifications.
coverage.fix: Provide certifications confirming satisfactory ICHAT and drug test results for all project personnel.

constraintViolations.proposalQuote: level 3 support and will also be working on the project who would most likely need to access state environments.
constraintViolations.violation: The proposal requests access to State environments for personnel located in Australia and New Zealand, violating the offshore access prohibition.
constraintViolations.fix: Commit that all personnel accessing State environments and systems will be physically located within the United States.

constraintViolations.proposalQuote: We have team members in Australia and New Zealand who perform level 3 support
constraintViolations.violation: The proposal utilizes support and project personnel located in Australia and New Zealand, violating the ban on offshore resources.
constraintViolations.fix: Ensure all project personnel and support resources are based exclusively within the United States.

findings.proposalQuote: We can confirm that data storage is included in the costs to be provided to the State.
findings.explanation: The proposal defers commercial cost information rather than providing required pricing details.
findings.fix: Provide a complete itemized pricing schedule with total cost rather than stating figures are to be provided.

findings.proposalQuote: Develop project schedule with key milestones (including specified deliverables)
findings.explanation: Omitting milestone calendar dates and phase durations prevents the client from determining if the mandatory implementation deadline can be achieved.
findings.fix: Provide a project schedule populated with specific durations and calendar target dates for all deliverables.

findings.proposalQuote: QLIMS has been tested to handle 250 concurrent users. This is made possible through carefully selecting infrastructure which can scale infinitely
findings.explanation: Claiming that infrastructure scales infinitely without acknowledging operational bottlenecks or cost constraints creates unrealistic service expectations for the State.
findings.fix: Revise the statement to define specific, tested auto-scaling thresholds and parameters (e.g., up to 250 concurrent users within defined resource limits) rather than claiming infinite scalability.

suggestedWeights.reason: The State requires deep domain knowledge across diverse public health disciplines including clinical diagnostics, infectious disease, genomics, and toxicology.
The RFP sets forth dozens of detailed technical tables and functional requirements that must each be designated by capability and configuration need.
Clear pricing is required across software licensing, hardware, subcontractor costs, and ongoing training support.
The RFP establishes a hard implementation cap of 1.5 years and requires a detailed milestone schedule tied to SUITE methodologies.
The worksheet demands explicit responses and exception logs for every numbered requirement, legal certification, and interface specification.
Responses must maintain a professional and compliant tone aligned with State of Michigan procurement standards.
Bidders are explicitly instructed to identify the impacted risk for any customized or configured requirement across all functional areas.
